xg.definition: Expected goals. The probability a shot becomes a goal, given only the information the model is allowed to see.

tracking-data.definition: Positions of the players and the ball sampled many times a second. This is not the same thing as a list of tagged events.

event-data.definition: A log of discrete actions such as passes, carries, and shots, usually with a location. Freeze frames, when present, are a snapshot around one event, not a full tracking feed.

substitute-data.definition: A public dataset used in place of the data the paper actually fit. A page that does this must show the Rebuilt on substitute data callout and say what does not transfer.

epa.definition: Expected points added. The change in expected points from the start of a play to the end of it.

logistic-regression.definition: A model that writes the log-odds of a yes-or-no outcome as a straight-line sum of the inputs, then turns that sum back into a probability.

log-odds.definition: The natural log of p / (1 − p), where p is a probability. Logistic regression models this, not the probability itself.

wald-statistic.definition: A significance statistic. In this paper's Table 1 it is about the coefficient divided by its standard error.

p-value.definition: The chance of an effect this large if the coefficient were truly zero. The paper keeps a variable when this is below 0.05.

added-points.definition: 3 × (made − predicted probability), for one field goal. Made is 1 or 0. Positive means the kick beat the probability the model gave it.

icing.definition: A timeout called just before the kick. The paper counts a timeout by either coach. It did not find an effect, and this page does not rebuild that test.

situational-pressure.definition: Score margin and time left, combined into a pressure level. The paper's Table A.1 tries several versions. None were significant, and this page does not rebuild them.

artificial-turf.definition: Any playing surface whose nflverse label is not grass. On this page that includes fieldturf and, because the label is not grass, Heinz Field's dessograss.

altitude-flag.definition: A game at 4,000 feet or above. In 2000–2011 that is Denver, plus the 2 October 2005 game in Mexico City (nflverse game_id 2005_04_SF_ARI).

nflverse.definition: An open, community-maintained NFL play-by-play dataset, licensed CC-BY-4.0. It is not the ArmchairAnalysis file this paper fit.

epv.definition: Expected possession value. A number for how a possession is expected to end, updated as the players and the ball move.

big-data-bowl.definition: The NFL's public analytics competition. Some years release player-tracking files that a paper can be rebuilt on directly.

statcast.definition: MLB's tracking of the ball and the players. Baseball Savant publishes a public slice of it, including pitch-level and batted-ball fields.
